problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable objectives f:E→ℝ, with no convexity requirement. A global lower bound ℓ exists with f(x0)−ℓ≤Δ; attainment is not required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CurvatureAlignedNoiseNonconvex.lean: spec.admissible, gradient existence and lower-bound clauses.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns g(x,ξ) with E[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x). Seeds are independent with a common distribution. The oracle supplies gradient samples only. All Params, including Lg, Lξ, σ, Δ, ε and x0, are public; f, Q and the sampling distribution are hidden.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: A hidden field of continuous linear operators Q(x) satisfies f(x+u)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),u⟩+⟨Q(x)u,u⟩/2 for every x,u, and ⟨Q(x)∇f(x),∇f(x)⟩≤Lg‖∇f(x)‖². No uniform operator-norm bound is stipulated.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CurvatureAlignedNoiseNonconvex.lean: spec.admissible, Q witness and two curvature inequalities.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For e(x,ξ)=g(x,ξ)−∇f(x), E‖e(x,ξ)‖²≤σ² uniformly in x. Joint measurability and the stated first and second moment integrability conditions are required; no light-tail condition is imposed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CurvatureAlignedNoiseNonconvex.lean: spec.admissible, measurability, integrability, unbiasedness and variance clauses.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel measurable structure. Accuracy and variance use its induced norm.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CurvatureAlignedNoiseNonconvex.lean: Params.normedE, innerE, finiteE, measurableE and borelE.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Noise curvature is controlled separately from gradient curvature: E⟨Q(x)e(x,ξ),e(x,ξ)⟩≤Lξ E‖e(x,ξ)‖², with the quadratic form integrable. Public parameters satisfy Lg>0, Lξ≥0, σ≥0, Δ≥0 and ε>0; Lξ may vanish despite nonzero variance.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CurvatureAlignedNoiseNonconvex.lean: spec.valid and final two spec.admissible clauses.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The output X∈E must be measurable, ‖∇f(X)‖ must be integrable, and E‖∇f(X)‖≤ε. This is the first power of the norm; no last-iterate requirement is imposed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over algorithm randomness and the oracle seed sequence under their product law. The extracted budget is a fixed cap of ⌈4LgΔ/ε²+8Lξσ²Δ/ε⁴⌉₊+1 stochastic-gradient calls.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CurvatureAlignedNoiseNonconvex.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence and execute; supplied OracleTemplate.CurvatureAligned.result budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation separates gradient-direction curvature from expected noise curvature through a hidden, point-dependent quadratic upper model. These assumptions are more specialized than the standard single-smoothness-constant stochastic nonconvex benchmark. Repository proofs and implementations were not inspected; the absence of a qualifying verified reference does not establish novelty.

descriptionHtml:
Nonconvex Optimization with Curvature-Aligned Noise

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. The objective admits global quadratic upper models with bounded curvature along its gradient and a bounded initial gap to a lower bound. The oracle returns an unbiased stochastic gradient at each query, using independent, identically distributed samples. Its noise has bounded variance and bounded expected curvature relative to its second moment. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with E∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε, where expectation includes oracle and independent algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Ef(x). Write ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ for the inner product and ∥⋅∥ for its induced norm. Fix a starting point x0∈E and parameters Lg>0,Lξ≥0,σ≥0,Δ≥0,ε>0. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, x0, and all five parameters; the objective and oracle distribution are accessed through oracle replies.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Quadratic upper models). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere. There exists a family of continuous linear maps Q(x):E→E such that, for every x,u∈E, f(x+u)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),u⟩+12⟨Q(x)u,u⟩,⟨Q(x)∇f(x),∇f(x)⟩≤Lg∥∇f(x)∥2.

Assumption 2 (Initial objective gap). There exists flow∈R such that f(x)≥flowfor every x∈E,f(x0)−flow≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Unbiased curvature-aligned noise). There exist a probability measure ν on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. Define the noise by ζ(x,ω)=g(x,ω)−∇f(x). For every fixed x∈E, the map g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable under ν, and both ∥ζ(x,⋅)∥2 and ⟨Q(x)ζ(x,⋅),ζ(x,⋅)⟩ are integrable under ν. For ω∼ν, they satisfy Eω∼ν[g(x,ω)]=∇f(x),Eω∼ν∥ζ(x,ω)∥2≤σ2,Eω∼ν⟨Q(x)ζ(x,ω),ζ(x,ω)⟩≤LξEω∼ν∥ζ(x,ω)∥2. At call k≥0, a query x∈E returns g(x,ξk), where the measurable sample variables (ξk)k≥0 are mutually independent and each has law ν. The algorithm’s randomness is independent of the entire sample sequence.

Queries may be made at any point of E. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its gradient norm must be integrable, and it must satisfy EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the oracle samples and the algorithm’s randomness.

comparisonHtml:
On a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, f is differentiable, f≥flow, and f(x0)−flow≤Δ. For every x,u, a linear map Q(x) satisfies f(x+u)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),u⟩+12⟨Q(x)u,u⟩ and ⟨Q(x)∇f(x),∇f(x)⟩≤Lg∥∇f(x)∥2. The jointly measurable oracle g uses IID samples with law P0, is integrable and unbiased, and has integrable noise moments satisfying EP0∥ζ∥2≤σ2 and EP0⟨Q(x)ζ,ζ⟩≤LξEP0∥ζ∥2. Here Lg>0, Lξ,σ,Δ≥0, ε>0. Target: measurable output with integrable gradient norm and ∫∥∇f(x^)∥dP≤ε. (1) constructs constant-step SGD with a uniformly random iterate; the setup imposes no algorithm restriction. Prior costs are converted from expected squared-gradient accuracy to this target.

Curvature-aligned stochastic nonconvex optimization: CurvatureAlignedNoiseNonconvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) CurvatureAlignedSgdNonconvex (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) O(1+LgΔε2+Lξσ2Δε4)
(2) Randomized SGD (Ghadimi and Lan 2013, Cor. 2.2). Special case: L-Lipschitz gradient. O(1+LΔε2+Lσ2Δε4) (1): Lg,Lξ replace L. For Lg,Lξ≤L, noise-dominated costs improve by Ω(L/Lξ) when Lξσ2≥Lgε2 and Lξσ2Δ/ε4≥1. Scope: no Lipschitz-gradient requirement. Accuracy exponents unchanged; formally verified refinement. (1)’s sharper constants require certified global Q and noise alignment; a local Hessian alone is insufficient.
(3) SGD (Liu et al. 2025, Thm. D.3). Special case: ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥D−1≤∥x−y∥D, D=diag(L)>0, Eζi2≤σi2. O(1+∥L∥∞Δε2+∥L∥∞∥σ∥22Δε4), batch size 1. (1): for admissible Q=diag(L), Lg≤∥L∥∞, σ2=∥σ∥22, Lξσ2=S, noise coefficient becomes S. Gain ∥L∥∞∥σ∥22/S when SΔ/ε4≥max{1,∥L∥∞Δ/ε2}, potentially d-fold. Scope: state-dependent, nondiagonal Q.

Abbr: Costs count individual stochastic-gradient calls. ζ=g(x,ω)−∇f(x); P is the execution probability law, including output randomization; Δ bounds the initial objective gap. L=(Li)i=1d, σ=(σi)i=1d, S=∑iLiσi2, ∥v∥D2=v⊤Dv.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.CurvatureAlignedNoiseNonconvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  Lg : ℝ
  Lξ : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.finiteE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.Lg ∧ 0 ≤ q.Lξ ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (P0 : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω))
      (Q : q.E → q.E →L[ℝ] q.E),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
      (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (P0 : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, x) seed => g x seed } ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x u, f (x + u) ≤ f x + ⟪gradient f x, u⟫ + ⟪Q x u, u⟫ / 2) ∧
    (∀ x, ⟪Q x (gradient f x), gradient f x⟫ ≤ q.Lg * ‖gradient f x‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∃ lower : ℝ, (∀ x, lower ≤ f x) ∧ f q.x0 - lower ≤ q.Δ) ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (g x) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂(P0 : Measure _) = gradient f x) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2 ∂(P0 : Measure _) ≤ q.σ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ⟪Q x (g x ω - gradient f x), g x ω - gradient f x⟫)
      (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, ⟪Q x (g x ω - gradient f x), g x ω - gradient f x⟫ ∂(P0 : Measure _) ≤
      q.Lξ * ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2 ∂(P0 : Measure _))
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.CurvatureAlignedNoiseNonconvex
